answer_text:
The poles of \(\cot^2(z)\) occur where \(\sin z = 0\), i.e.

\[
z = n\pi, \qquad n \in \mathbb{Z}.
\]

Let \(w = z - n\pi\). Since \(\cot(z)\) has period \(\pi\),

\[
\cot^2(z) = \cot^2(w).
\]

Near \(w=0\),

\[
\cot w = \frac{1}{w} - \frac{w}{3} + O(w^3).
\]

Therefore,

\[
\cot^2 w
= \left(\frac{1}{w} - \frac{w}{3} + O(w^3)\right)^2
= \frac{1}{w^2} - \frac{2}{3} + O(w^2).
\]

There is no \(1/w\) term in the Laurent expansion, so the residue at each pole is \(0\).

\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Res}(\cot^2 z, n\pi)=0 \quad \text{for all } n\in\mathbb{Z}}
\]
